definitions.explanation: A door or entrance at the back of a building, as opposed to the main entrance.
Figuratively, an unofficial or illegitimate way of achieving something, often implying bribery or unfair advantage.

examples.japanese: {裏口|うらぐち}から{入|はい}ってください。
examples.english: Please enter through the back door.

examples.japanese: {裏口|うらぐち}{入学|にゅうがく}は{問題|もんだい}になっている。
examples.english: Backdoor admissions have become a problem.
examples.notes: Refers to gaining admission through bribery or connections

examples.japanese: {正面|しょうめん}{玄関|げんかん}が{閉|し}まっていたので{裏口|うらぐち}を{使|つか}った。
examples.english: The front entrance was closed, so I used the back door.

examples.japanese: {裏口|うらぐち}から{荷物|にもつ}を{運|はこ}び{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I carried the luggage in through the back door.

examples.japanese: {裏口|うらぐち}で{仕事|しごと}を{取|と}るのはよくない。
examples.english: Getting work through backdoor connections is not good.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{裏口|うらぐち}から{政治|せいじ}の{世界|せかい}に{入|はい}ったと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It's said that he entered the world of politics through the back door.

notes:
USAGE: {裏口|うらぐち} has both literal and figurative meanings.

LITERAL:
・{裏口|うらぐち}から{入|はい}る (to enter from the back)
・{裏口|うらぐち}を{開|あ}ける (to open the back door)

FIGURATIVE (illicit means):
・{裏口|うらぐち}{入学|にゅうがく} (backdoor admission - through bribery/connections)
・{裏口|うらぐち}{営業|えいぎょう} (illicit business)

CONTRAST:
・{表口|おもてぐち}/{正面|しょうめん}{玄関|げんかん} - front entrance
・{勝手口|かってぐち} - kitchen entrance, service entrance
